plan.rationale: The frozen objective is ttft_ms on one infer() call of a single-process, single-GPU BF16 sdpa inference workload, so the open questions are host-side, not communication-side. The torch collector already ran and coverage.json shows complete attribution (34229/34229 kernels associated, 0 ambiguous forward sequences, 0 autograd ranges), so kernel-level GPU attribution needs no reinforcement. Communication-oriented collectors are excluded on capability evidence: nccl_tuning and collective_calibration have no collectives to observe (communication=not_applicable, 'single-device task'; a synthetic full-world SUM allreduce would be an unrelated reference experiment, not a lower bound or critical-path estimate for this task), and device_telemetry only yields device-wide NVML PCIe/utilization/memory readings with native windows that cannot be attributed to the prefill/argmax boundary of a GPU-resident-inputs invocation. nsys is available but adds nothing here: no overlap, graph-tracing, or attribution question remains, and nsys timelines alone would not separate transfer components or prove identity even if they did. execution_timeline is selected to obtain a separate plain trace with CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, the explicit boundary synchronize, per-device busy/idle intervals, and clock alignment bounds, which determines whether TTFT is GPU-compute-bound or host-dispatch-gap-bound (its optional gradient callbacks are not applicable to this inference workload). python_runtime is selected to investigate host dispatch and binding costs of the generate/forward loop under the legacy binding backend, accepted as a perturbing diagnostic whose times are not clean performance scores. candidate_diagnostics is deferred since no optimization candidates exist at collection time. Unavailable dimensions are listed with their observed reasons rather than guessed.
